title: Claude Code vs Codex CLI — The Honest Comparison (2026)
summary: Claude Code vs Codex CLI comparison with a self-run expense-tracker test; several cited survey figures look unsupported.

assertions.quote: Claude Code consumed 6.1 million tokens ... Codex CLI consumed 1.4 million tokens

verdicts.note: Several practitioner comparisons report lower token use for Codex, but results vary by task, model and settings; a single run isn't evidence.

On the same 111 SWE-rebench tasks Codex (GPT-5.6 Sol) used about 2.07M tokens per problem against 3.34M for Claude Code (Fable 5), roughly 38% fewer: fewer, but not by a wide multiple, and with different models inside each tool.

assertions.quote: In blind code reviews across 500 developers, Claude Code's output was preferred 67% of the time

verdicts.note: The cited 500-developer blind review has no traceable source; quality comparisons swing with each model release.

assertions.quote: Codex's kernel sandbox cannot. It's enforced by the operating system

verdicts.note: Codex does use Seatbelt/Landlock sandboxing; Claude Code added an OS-level sandbox option in late 2025, so the contrast is outdated.

assertions.quote: The best developers in 2026 aren't choosing one tool. They're using both

verdicts.note: Developer surveys (e.g. Stack Overflow 2025) show many use multiple AI tools concurrently.
